items.headline: Singapore Exchange full-year turnover hits S$455.7 billion, an 18-year high
items.summary: SGX reported total securities turnover jumped 35% to S$455.7 billion in FY2026, with securities daily average value up 35% to S$1.8 billion, the highest in 18 years.

items.headline: Man, 24, jailed 22 months for underage sex with a girl he vowed to marry
items.summary: A Singaporean, now 26, was jailed 22 months after pleading guilty to three of seven charges over sex with a 14-year-old he said he would marry at 18.

items.headline: Team Singapore athlete charged with rape of a 12-year-old, carding suspended
items.summary: A national athlete faces two rape charges over a 12-year-old girl met online; he was 17 at the time. Sports bodies suspended his carding support.

items.headline: Man, 40, charged over hoax bomb threats to the HTX building and Parliament House
items.summary: Koh Jye Shyang faces two counts of communicating false information after a claimed bomb at HTX and an email to the PMO alleging a bomb at Parliament House. No devices found.

items.headline: India's retail inflation climbs to 4.38% in June, breaching the RBI's target
items.summary: June CPI rose to 4.38%, above the RBI's 4% target for the first time in about 17 months, on food and fuel costs, but within the 2-6% band.

items.headline: Update: Rupee slides toward a record low as the Hormuz oil spike hits Indian markets
items.summary: The rupee weakened to about 95.70 per dollar and the Nifty 50 slipped below 24,000 as US-Iran fighting lifted Brent above $79; the RBI intervened.

items.headline: State Bank of India raises over $1.5 billion via an overseas-citizen deposit scheme
items.summary: SBI raised more than $1.5 billion from foreign-currency deposits under a special programme for overseas Indians launched last month, to shore up dollar inflows.

items.headline: Foreign funds buy $1.2 billion of Indian equities in a week despite Middle East jitters
items.summary: Global funds made net purchases of about $1.2 billion of Indian stocks over the week, cushioning oil-driven headwinds from the Hormuz crisis.

items.headline: Andy Burnham set to become UK prime minister on 20 July as Labour MPs rally behind him
items.summary: The Greater Manchester mayor won nominations from the large majority of Labour's 403 MPs after Starmer's resignation; he is expected to be confirmed leader Friday and take office 20 July.

items.headline: Burnham signals he will keep Reeves's fiscal rules but reshuffle the cabinet
items.summary: Burnham has said he will keep Labour's manifesto pledges and Reeves's fiscal rules, even as reports suggest Reeves leaves the Treasury and Wes Streeting is tipped as a successor.

items.headline: Ofwat finds Severn Trent breached wastewater duties but imposes no fine
items.summary: Ofwat ruled Severn Trent had serious monitoring failings but declined to fine it, citing the £98m already spent on fixes; the wider probe has yielded over £300m in penalties.

items.headline: Update: Trump declares the US 'guardian' of Hormuz, imposing a 20% cargo toll
items.summary: Declaring the ceasefire over, Trump said the US would reimpose a blockade of Iranian ports and charge 20% on Hormuz cargo; Iran's FM disputed it as Brent topped $83.

items.headline: Ukraine and nine nations launch a coalition against Russian ballistic missiles
items.summary: At a Paris summit Zelenskyy and nine European leaders unveiled a shared anti-ballistic-missile effort backing Ukraine's 'Freyja' system; Russia struck Kyiv during the talks.

items.headline: Japan to build a new national intelligence agency to counter China, Russia and North Korea
items.summary: Tokyo announced a new national intelligence agency to coordinate capabilities, citing espionage threats from China, Russia and North Korea.

items.headline: DR Congo's Ebola deaths reach 600 as the outbreak spreads to a fourth province
items.summary: Confirmed deaths reached 600 and cases 1,759 across Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu, with a new case in Haut-Uele; health workers in Ituri walked off the job.

items.headline: Brazil braces for a 15 July US decision on 25% Section 301 tariffs
items.summary: The USTR faces a 15 July deadline on a 25% Section 301 tariff on Brazilian goods over digital-trade and IP rules; Lula says Brazil cannot accept such treatment.

items.headline: Intel to invest €5 billion to expand its Ireland hub in the AI chip race
items.summary: Intel will spend about €5 billion ($5.7bn) to expand its Ireland plant as it tries to regain process leadership amid surging AI demand.

items.headline: General Fusion debuts on the Nasdaq as the first publicly traded fusion company
items.summary: General Fusion began trading as GFUZ after merging with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp. III, the first publicly listed pure-play fusion firm, with ~$150m in cash.

items.headline: Xi Jinping to deliver his first keynote at China's World AI Conference in Shanghai
items.summary: Xi will address the 2026 World AI Conference in Shanghai on 17 July, his first appearance since 2018, promoting a proposed World AI Cooperation Organization.

items.headline: Nadella warns companies 'pay for intelligence twice' when adopting AI
items.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella argued firms pay for AI in tokens and again by handing over proprietary knowledge, urging them to retain data ownership.

items.headline: Update: Apple's trade-secret lawsuit threatens OpenAI's bid to rival the iPhone
items.summary: Apple's 10 July suit alleges 400+ ex-staff including Tang Tan took IP to OpenAI, a case that could disrupt OpenAI's Jony Ive-led hardware plans.

items.headline: TSMC posts record second-quarter revenue, up 36%, on surging AI-chip demand
items.summary: TSMC reported Q2 revenue of about T$1.27 trillion (~$39.6bn), up 36% and beating estimates, with June sales up 68%.

items.headline: SK Hynix raises $26.5 billion in the largest-ever foreign listing on a US exchange
items.summary: SK Hynix sold 177.9m ADRs at $149 to raise $26.5bn, the biggest US debut by a foreign company, topping Alibaba's 2014 IPO.

items.headline: AkzoNobel rejects Nippon Paint's $8.6 billion bid for its decorative-paints unit
items.summary: AkzoNobel's board rejected Nippon Paint's €7.5bn ($8.6bn) offer as significantly undervaluing the unit and reaffirmed its Axalta merger.

items.headline: Wall Street slides and gold sinks as Trump reimposes a Hormuz shipping toll
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 0.79% to 7,515.34 and the Nasdaq dropped 1.55% after Trump's 20% Hormuz tariff; gold slid 1.2% to ~$4,070 and the dollar index rose to 101.07.

items.headline: Circle jumps 13% after winning OCC approval for a national trust bank
items.summary: Circle rose about 13% after final OCC approval to establish Circle National Trust, a federally regulated bank for USDC digital-asset custody.

items.headline: 🏎️ Verstappen's Red Bull exit clause is active as his future dominates pre-Spa talk
items.summary: With Verstappen out of the title top two, his exit clause is live and his future is the key storyline into the Belgium-Hungary double-header; the Belgian GP runs 17-19 July.

items.headline: 🏎️ Ferrari surge into race week as Antonelli defends a 25-point championship lead
items.summary: Race week for the 19 July Belgian GP opens with Antonelli leading Russell by 25 points but Ferrari closing after two wins in three races, and Aston Martin debuting a Newey aero package.

items.headline: 🎾 Zverev climbs to World No. 2 past the injured Alcaraz after his Wimbledon final run
items.summary: New ATP rankings see Zverev overtake the injured Alcaraz for No. 2 on his final run, while champion Sinner extends his No. 1 lead to nearly 5,000 points.

items.headline: 🎾 Noskova and Muchova crack the WTA top 10 after their Wimbledon breakthrough
items.summary: Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova rose to a career-high No. 7 and beaten finalist Karolina Muchova also reached a new career high inside the top 10.

items.headline: 🏏 Rohit, Kohli and Bumrah return as India face England in the ODI series opener
items.summary: India's ODI series at Edgbaston begins with Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and Jasprit Bumrah recalled after a losing T20I campaign, possibly Rohit and Kohli's last England tour.

items.headline: Hubble finds the first of a star cluster's long-sought 'missing' black holes
items.summary: Astronomers found oMEGACat BH-2, a 4.46-solar-mass black hole orbiting a star in Omega Centauri, the longest-period black-hole binary known, in Hubble and Webb data.

items.headline: An undersea observatory records Earth's oceanic crust being born in real time
items.summary: Instruments near Amsterdam Island captured a full seafloor-spreading episode at the Southeast Indian Ridge, magma tearing the seafloor open in under two hours with ~4m subsidence.

items.headline: Webb detects the first atmosphere on a planet orbiting a dead star
items.summary: JWST read the atmosphere of WD 1856 b, a Jupiter-sized world orbiting a white dwarf, finding methane and hazy aerosols, the first atmosphere seen on a planet transiting a white dwarf.

items.headline: Gene therapy restores more hearing on a second dose, beating immune antibodies
items.summary: In a Nature Medicine trial, four congenitally deaf patients re-dosed with OTOF gene therapy in the second ear overcame neutralising antibodies and gained further hearing.

items.headline: Great apes and humans laugh in the same rhythm, hinting at ancient vocal control
items.summary: Comparing tickle-induced laughter across great apes, researchers found evenly spaced rhythms present in our last common ancestor, dating complex vocal control to ~15 million years ago.

fun_fact.headline: Tardigrades can survive the open vacuum of space
fun_fact.body: Tardigrades ('water bears') can expel almost all their body water into a dormant 'tun' and survive near absolute zero, boiling, and deep-ocean pressures. In 2007 the ESA's FOTON-M3 mission exposed live tardigrades to the vacuum of space and many survived, some even withstanding solar radiation before revival on Earth.

puzzle.title: The Slow Drinker
puzzle.body: Two friends order the same iced cocktail from one pitcher; one gulps hers and is fine, the other sips his slowly and dies. Both glasses and the pitcher held the same poison. How did the fast drinker survive?
puzzle.approach: Everything stated is literally true; ask what changed between the glasses over time.
puzzle.answer: The poison was frozen into the ice cubes. The fast drinker finished before the ice melted; the slow drinker's melting ice released the poison over half an hour.

word_puzzle.title: Four Sides, Two Words
word_puzzle.body: Letter Boxed square (Top: P O A, Right: R C I, Bottom: L M E, Left: T S N). Use all 12 letters; consecutive letters from different sides; each word starts with the last letter of the previous. Solve in two words.
word_puzzle.approach: Chain two long words covering all twelve letters.
